answer: activate is one operational-mode verb with several sub-parameters: swimage (activates the currently installable image, implies a system restart, db-action auto|empty-db|upgrade-db|rollback default auto), database (activates the currently inactive database, restart-type cold|warm default cold, sanity-check-override default false), location-led (entity is a chassis or card, led-mode flash|solid default flash, timeout 0..120 s default 0 meaning no timeout, only one test at a time), eqpt-fw (resource plus fw-image-name), krp (installs a Key Replacement Package), otdr, otdr-fiber-check, loopback (WSS loopback on an NMC) and activate-file. Unless -f is given you must confirm. The database-snapshot case has its own command: activate-snapshot db-instance <string> db-paraphrase <string> [sanity-check-override true|false], db-instance default temp, and a snapshot must already have been taken.

Per card: show capabilities-<name>, where name is the card name; it retrieves that card's capabilities (Operational and Candidate Configuration mode). Photonic layer: show l0-capabilities, which shows the capability details for the node's Layer 0 functions; it takes no parameters. Add/drop: show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs] - max-degrees is the maximum number of degrees (20, uint8; 0 if not supported, and degrees exist only on OADM node types, ILA is 0 by convention because it has just two fixed directions), max-adgs is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups (110, uint8; 0 if not supported, OADM node types only). The maximum degree count is the maximum 'working' degree-number, not necessarily a supported deployment configuration.

Controller only: show controller-card-<name> [redundancy-status] [redundancy-standby-status] [number-of-switchover-events] [time-of-last-switchover] [additional-details]. redundancy-status is active|standby|not-in-service (default not-in-service); redundancy-standby-status is ready-synchronized, not-ready-synchronizing (default), not-ready-synchronize-fail, lock-out or card-not-present; switchover count and timestamp are visible only on the active controller. Any card in the shelf: card, the card-base object common to all card types, with required-type, required-subtype, card-mode, chassis-name, slot-name, power-profile, admin-state, last-reboot-reason and last-reboot-time. What a card model supports: show supported-card-<card-type>, giving node-type-compatibility (all|ILA|OADM), category (controller, line-card, fan, power-supply, carrier-card, blank, other), card-width, max-power-draw, location-led-support and support-serdes-config (default false).

macsec-entity is MACsec on an Ethernet facility: add/set/show/delete macsec-entity-<name> with supporting-facility (e.g. ethernet-6-3-3), enabled default true, link-security-control must-secure|should-secure default must-secure, replay-protection enable|disable, replay-protection-window 0..4294967295 default 0, and read-only negotiated-cipher-suite. secure-entity is L1/optical-line encryption: add secure-entity-<name> supporting-facility <value> remote-secure-entity <value> (the remote optical carrier on G40, remote ODU on G30, or remote OTUFlex), enabled default false, re-key-frequency 3600..86400 s default 28800, re-key-fail-policy kill-traffic|continue-traffic default continue-traffic, traffic-kill-offset 0..86400 s default 0. Cipher terms: MACsec ones in mka-policy (macsec-cipher-suite, confidentiality-offset); optical ones in the show-only secure-entity-sa-proposal (encryption-algorithm aes-gcm-16, encryption-key-length key-length-256, integrity-algorithm none, dh-group ecp-521).

ase-idler-service is the per-card ASE idler filling function on the WSS: add/delete/set/show ase-idler-service-<name>, key attribute ase-idler-enable enabled|disabled (default disabled) which fills the unused and nmc-failed portions of the band, plus read-only ase-idler-state (ase-enabled, ase-partially-enabled, ase-faulted, ase-disabled, default ase-disabled) and function idler. ase-idler-source is the pump that generates the signal: set/show only, pump-enable enabled|disabled default disabled, target-output-power -3.00..20.50 dBm default 13, read-only pump-state, admin-state lock|unlock|maintenance default unlock, function ase-idler-source. sw-service does not belong with them: show sw-service-<sv-name> / show sw-services lists software services and containers on the node, with state off|ok|fail, cpu-usage, memory-usage, uptime, last-start-time and reboot-count.

No. change-ztp-mode [-f] [ztp-mode=]enabled|disabled toggles Zero Touch Provisioning; change-ztp-mode enabled starts ZTP, reverts the database to the factory default and triggers a system reboot, while disabled stops ZTP even if it is already running. Operational mode, prompts unless -f; check with show ztp. clear [-f] recover-mode clears the recover-mode flag, confirming the current configuration as is, re-enabling communication with the line cards and potentially reconfiguring traffic settings, so it may be traffic impacting; no parameters, prompts unless -f. The carrier-mode commands are read-only by contrast: show supported-carrier-mode-<name>/<carrier-mode> lists supported modes (capacity, client-mode ethernet|ethernet-otn, baud-rate, application, compatibility-id, status), and show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode> adds actual-carrier-mode, sop-tracking-mode and candidate-subtypes.

State: show third-party-app-<app-name> (also show third-party-app-info-<location-id>/<app-name>) gives state running|stopped|failed (default stopped) and enable true|false (default false; if enabled the app is started and restarts with the system, if disabled it is stopped), plus version, vendor, product, label and information (0..1024 chars). Firmware side: show third-party-fw-<fw-name> gives file-status valid|invalid|missing, path, version, crc, vendor, part-number, nsa-upgrade-version (versions from which upgrade is non-service-affecting), present-in-eqpt and applicable-eqpt (max 80 elements each). Clearing: clear [-f] app [app-name=]<value>, which prompts unless -f is given. To restart rather than clear, use appctl [app-name=]<value> [command=]restart|netls|exec [target=]<value> (default system) with optional parameters (max 50).

Per session: cli-session-config-<session-id>. set cli-session-config-<session-id> cli-lines <value> gives more rows for that login only; cli-lines is 10..1000, default 40, the rows shown before pausing (SPACEBAR resumes). Also cli-columns 80..4000 default 80, interactive-mode true|false default true (per session, not persistent) and display-timestamp default false. The protocol as a whole is cli: enabled default true (you cannot disable CLI from within a CLI session), port 1..65535 default 22, script-dir read-only, default-interactive-mode default true (new sessions only), show-alarm-columns default default-columns with global effect. The two system-configuration objects are config (show config [entity-id|entity-type], displaying non-default configuration recursively from the current scope) and configure (enters Candidate Configuration mode, target exclusive or shared, default exclusive, optionally from-default, from-script or from-commit).

The generic assignment is set: set [-f|-v] [<entity id>] <attribute> <value> [...] [<filter> ...]. It changes attributes of existing managed entities, needs at least one attribute-value pair from the same entity, supports wildcards (card-*, port-1-4-*) and ranges or lists (card-1-[1..4], interface-[DCN,CRAFT]), and asks for confirmation when the request may be traffic impacting or implicitly affects multiple instances; -v validates, -f forces. The set- prefixed ones are separate operations: set-alarm-state [state=]<value> [[acknowledge-text=]<value>] (all-alarms | [alarm-id-list=]<value>...) changes the operator state of alarms (none, ack, close; state is mandatory; 1 to 10 alarm ids; acknowledge-text 0..256 chars), and set-time [new-time=]<value> changes the system time, only applicable when the time-source is manual (NTP not enabled), in ISO 8601 form such as 2021-02-06T11:16:58Z or with +/-hh:mm. The one ending in -set is named-value-set-<db-entry-name>/<named-value-set-name>, a data object whose value is a string 1..1024.

mc is the Media Channel, a user-creatable spectrum slot on an OMS: add mc-<name> parent-oms <value> lower-frequency <value> upper-frequency <value> in MHz, with center-frequency and slot-width calculated by the system and auto-delete disabled by default. nmc is the Network Media Channel, the carrier inside it: add nmc-<name> parent-facility <value> center-frequency <value>, center-frequency 190650000..196700000 MHz, width 15000..200000 MHz default 35000 (set to the 3 dB signal bandwidth matching the transponder baud rate). For both, the supporting card must be part of a Degree, not an ADG. The fillers are show-only objects the system creates for unused spectrum: mc-f reports lower-frequency, upper-frequency and slot-width; nmc-f reports alloc- and actual- lower/upper frequency and bandwidth (alloc-bandwidth default 75000 MHz), power-actual-tx/rx and monitoring-state, and allows only admin-state and alarm-report-control to be set.

What runs the scan: activate otdr [entity=]<port> [[otdr-file-prefix=]<value>], or activate otdr-fiber-check [entity=]<ots-r-id> for a manual OTDR-based fiber check (used when automatic OTDR is disabled; runs up to 3 tests and errors if a scan is already in progress). Where you tune it: otdr-ptp - otdr-range auto or 0..300.0 km, otdr-pulse-width auto or 10..20000 ns, otdr-measurement-speed fast|medium|slow|precision|auto|high-precision (default auto), otdr-ior auto or 1.0..2.0, otdr-fiber-type (auto, SSMF, SMF-ULL, LEAF...), otdr-resolution auto or 0.4..100.0, otdr-direction-mode default counter-prop-in-service, peak-power auto or 5..14.5, launching-fiber-length 0..50 m default 0. Where the answer comes out: otdr-ptp otdr-fiber-break-distance (break distance in km, not-available if none found), otdr-last-measurement and otdr-last-measurement-file (the .sor file). Live status is on otdr: otdr-state not-available|idle|measuring|finished|fail, otdr-measurement-port, otdr-measurement-direction, otdr-error.

The entry that keeps coming back is DHCP-assigned. Each dns-server-<address> has origin: dhcp means the address was assigned by a DHCP server, manual means it was configured by hand; default manual. Convert it with set dns-server-<address> origin manual. What the node accepts at all is dns assignment-method, which is manual, dhcp or both, default both; set it to manual to stop DHCP-learned servers being installed. dns also has enabled (default true) and search (must contain at least one dot, 0..64 chars, cleared with an empty string). For the relay two things must line up: global dhcp-relay has mode disabled|ipv4|ipv6, default disabled, plus server-address (at least one address must be configured when enabled); and per interface if-dhcp-relay-<if-name> dhcp-relay-enabled true|false, default false, which obeys the global dhcp-relay settings. A relay that does nothing usually means mode is still disabled or the interface flag is still false.

clear [-f] system [[action=]<value>] [[restart-behavior=]<value>] [type=]<value> [[target=]<value>] wipes the system and resets it to factory configuration, doing a secure wipe of the system data. The three types are: factory-reset, which resets the system or a particular equipment to factory configuration, stopping target traffic services and removing the respective files and user configurations, and may imply loss of connectivity; full-wipe, which cleans the entire system and reinstalls the software on the controller and line cards, removing all files, configurations and software, requiring a base software reinstall from ONIE to recover; and inactive, which only clears the inactive software partition and so leaves the running system, its data and its configuration in place. target may be the whole system (the default) or a chassis/card AID; restart-behavior is restart (default) or shutdown. factory-reset with shutdown is not supported on L0 cards, and factory-reset does not take effect on G30 OCC2T/OCC2E. For a simple database wipe use clear database.

Read show unprovisioned-inventory-<chassis-serial-number>/<slot-name>, which lists inventory detected but not yet accepted by the Node Controller in a multi-chassis configuration. It reports hardware-version, actual-type, actual-subtype, sw-support-revision, PON, serial-number (1..16 chars), clei, vendor, part-number, manufacture-date and detection-timestamp, the last being when the Node Controller last detected the unprovisioned equipment; if the equipment is the chassis itself the slot-name is empty. Pair it with show nct-connection-<src-port>/<dst-port>, which shows the dynamically discovered links between NCT ports in a multi-chassis NE and gives src-chassis, dst-chassis and src-chassis-state/dst-chassis-state, each node controller, provisioned or unprovisioned. Ports on a commissioned chassis appear as the port AID, ports on an unprovisioned chassis as <chassis-serial-number>-<slot>-NCT-<id>.

The attribute is amplifier control-mode: auto-max-pw (the auto mode targeting maximum output power, and the default) or manual, where you set the gain with gain-target (0..40 dB, default 0.0, for constant-gain mode). amp-control-support reports whether auto is offered at all (auto, or manual-only). In auto mode bias the result with gain-adjustment (-20.00..20.00 dB, default 0, only on amplifiers with function pa or inline). gain-range-control follows control-mode: manual forces it to manual, auto-max-pw forces it to auto. What stops output entirely: amplifier-enable disabled (the default) - output also depends on the OSC signal for ILA node type and on OMS facilities plus an existing OXcon for OADM; forced-shutdown true (dual-band cards); admin-state lock; and an input OLOS, which after olos-shutdown-soak-timer (0..2000 ms, default 0) triggers shutdown unless olos-shutdown-disable is true. amplifier-mode is always constant-gain.

Which member is live: show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name> state, which is active, standby, available or unknown, together with role (working or protection) and transport-entity. At group level show protection-group-<name> pg-state gives no-request, forced-to-working/protection, manual-to-working/protection, sf-on-working/protection, sd-on-working/protection, wait-to-restore, protection-lockout, frozen, do-not-revert or unavailable (default), plus last-switch-trigger and remaining-wtr. The switch behaviour settings are all on protection-group: protection-type y-cable|snc-n default y-cable, switching-mode unidirectional|bidirectional default unidirectional, reversion-mode revertive|non-revertive default non-revertive, hold-off-timer 0..10000 ms default 0, wtr-timer 60..720 s default 300 (revertive only), and the triggers client-side-olos-trigger, client-side-sd-trigger, network-side-csf-trigger and network-side-sd-trigger, all disabled by default. Operate a switch with protection-switch [-f] operation-type=force|lockout|manual|release.

Trigger with verify [-f] [type-select=]fiber-connection [[target-select=]<port-id>] [allow-switching]. With no port-id all paths are verified; allow-switching defaults to false - true lets CableID initiate OPSM switching so both active and inactive paths are checked, false checks active paths only. Pre-condition: equipment-policies cable-id-control must be enabled. It prompts unless -f, is non-blocking, and raises CID-verification-in-progress against the NE until all queued requests finish. Watch progress with show cable-id-status: cable-id-state idle|running-incl-switching|running-no-switching, and test-progress as 'N out of M completed'. Per-pair results are in show cable-id-path-<name>: last-test-status not-verified|pass|fail in each direction, path-status enabled|disabled, last-test-qualifier up-to-date|out-dated, last-test-timestamp, and additional-info (Cable-ID TxLOS, RxLOS, Cable-ID-MISMATCH for a misconnected fibre, RxLOF, power out-of-range, timeout). show -r adds the supporting fiber connections; abort with terminate cable-id.

Where authentication is sent is decided by aaa-server: add/set aaa-server-<server-name> protocol-supported RADIUS|TACACSPLUS (default RADIUS), server-address, server-priority 1..10, enabled true|false (default true), role-supported (authentication, authorization, accounting by default), shared-secret (max 64 characters, longer is rejected, shown as *), source-ip for RADIUS communications, and ports server-port default 49, server-port-authentication default 1812, server-port-accounting default 1813. Whether remote AAA is consulted at all is security-policies aaa-authentication-method: local-only (default), local-first-then-remote, remote-first-then-local, or remote-unavailable-then-local. What happens when the server does not answer is governed by aaa-server timeout (1..90 s, default 5) and retry (0..5), with total wait timeout x (retry + 1) required to be under 5 minutes. show aaa-statistics-<server-name> counts connection-failures, which include unavailable servers and timeouts.

For key-based login by the automation account use ssh-authorized-key: add ssh-authorized-key-<user-name>/<key-id> public-key <value> [label <value>]. Each entry holds a trusted public key for SSHv2 user authentication; user-name 0..32 chars (local or remote user), key-id 1..64, public-key OpenSSH/PEM up to 2048 chars, public-key-algorithm read-only (ecdsa-sha2-nistp256/384/521, ssh-rsa2048/3072/4096). Also set security-policies ssh-authentication-method to public-key or public-key-or-password (default password). For the remote host the node copies files to, use ssh-known-host: add ssh-known-host-<id> address <value> public-key-algorithm <value> public-key <value>, algorithms as above plus ssh-ed25519 (from R9.0); enforcement is security-policies ssh-strict-host-key-checking, strict or relaxed, default relaxed. The node's own identity is ssh-host-key (show-only, one per algorithm), generated by ssh-keygen [-b=<key-length>] [-l=<label>] [-t=rsa|ecdsa|ed25519], default rsa.

The key agreement policy lives in mka-policy: add/set mka-policy-<name> with key-server-priority (used by MKA to select the key server), macsec-cipher-suite (cipher suites for Secure Association Key derivation) and confidentiality-offset (octets of the Ethernet frame sent unencrypted). It is referenced from the entity via macsec-mka: set macsec-mka-<name> mka-policy <value>, which also carries connectivity-association-key and connectivity-association-key-name (0..64 chars), psk-lifetime/psk-expiration-warning 1..173 days default 14, psk-lifetime-enable, and read-only is-key-server (default false). Session key rollover is mka-policy sak-rekey-interval, in seconds, range 0 or 30..65535, default 30 s. Watch the channels with show sc-tx-<name>/<index> and show sc-rx-<name>/<index>: sci-tx/sci-rx (16-char hex SCI), state in-use or not-in-use as returned by the MKA stack, association-number, key-identifier and next-packet-number. macsec-entity also reports negotiated-cipher-suite.

NETCONF: set/show netconf - enabled default true (you cannot disable NETCONF from within a NETCONF session), port default 830 (range 1..65535, over ssh), hello-timeout 1..3600 s default 2 (the session is dropped if no hello PDU is exchanged in that time), annotate-cli-name default false. gNMI/gRPC: set/show grpc - enabled default true, port default 50051, gnmi-get-encoding-granularity per-path or per-object, default per-object. Neither is off out of the box. RESTCONF is the one with a piece disabled by default: enabled default true and https-enabled default true on https-port 8181, but http-enabled defaults to false (HTTP access is not supported in secure mode) on http-port 8080, with cookie-timeout 1..300 minutes default 5 and read-only api-root. For reference the CLI itself listens on port 22. grpc is system managed and cannot be manually deleted.

restart [-h] [-f] [<resource-id>] [<type>] [<sub-component>] restarts a specific resource and prompts for confirmation unless -f is given. Omit resource-id and the active node controller card is restarted; omit type and a warm restart is done by default. So 'restart card-1-4' is warm: it reboots the card processor and is non service affecting, with connectivity regained within five minutes. cold reboots all components and sub-components and is service affecting (connectivity back within five minutes); shutdown gracefully shuts the card down. You cannot assume every card behaves the same - the guide states not all cards support all restart types, and gives counter-examples: a cold reboot of XMM4 is not service affecting but visibility is lost, while cold reboot of CHM6/UCM4 is service affecting; warm reboot of XMM4 is non-service affecting but loses visibility for 3 minutes. Restartable entities: card (cold, warm, shutdown), card sub-component (cold, warm), tom (cold only). List sub-components with show card resources.

Three things. First the global switch: set equipment-templates use-serdes-templates enabled (enabled/disabled, default disabled). Template application depends on this flag being true; enabling it does not retro-apply templates, they apply from that moment onward, and disabling it keeps the existing serdes configuration on all TOMs. Second a template keyed on part number: add serdes-template-<name> [tom-part-number <value>] [card-types-applicable <value>] [ports-applicable <value>], tom-part-number 1..16 chars, ports-applicable 'all' (the default consideration) or up to 20 port names such as T1, T10. Third the values: add serdes-template-entry-<serdes-template-name>/<entry-name> value <value>, one per serdes parameter (RxAmplitude, RxEQ, TxEQ, RxPreCursor, RxPostCursor, TxEQAdaptive). When a TOM with that part-number is plugged in the template is applied automatically; manual serdes settings are kept even if they deviate, and swapping in a TOM with a different part-number resets serdes and re-applies the new template. Force re-application with apply-template. Card support is shown by supported-card support-serdes-config (default false).

OTS, the Optical Transport Section, is the fibre span between nodes: fiber-type-tx/rx, fiber-length-tx/rx, span-loss-reference, span-loss-transmit/receive, external-attenuation-tx/rx, raman coefficients, target-power-setting, osc-compatibility osc-g30 (default) or osc-7100, osc-less, laser-safety-mode. OMS, the Optical Multiplex Section, is the multiplexed DWDM band on it: monitoring-mode (intrusive by default, not-monitored for ILA, integrated-equalization for hyperscale ILA), grid-mode (flexible by default, or fixed-50G-96ch, fixed-75G-64ch, fixed-100G-48ch, fixed-150G-40ch), lower-frequency 191300000 and upper-frequency 196150000 MHz, attenuation-control-mode-rx/tx default auto. OPS, the Optical Physical Section, is the individual physical port: role tributary, multi-carrier, general-purpose (default), ase-input or active-multi-carrier; input-psd-profile -30..-6 default -6. OSC carries the supervisory traffic: osc-mode OC3 (155 Mbit/s) or 1GE for HSC OLS, osc-control auto (default) or manual, target-output-power -2.5..4.5 dBm, voa-attenuation-target-rx 0..30 dB default 10, l0-comm-interface-type ipv4 or ipv6, lof-soak-timer short|long.

The behaviour is configured on trib-ptp, in tributary-disable-action: it defines what the node does towards the client equipment connected over the TOM when a line-side failure is observed. The default is laser-shut-off, so the node turns the client laser off. The alternatives insert a replacement signal instead: none, odu-ais, send-ais-1, send-gais, send-idles, send-lf, send-ms-ais, and send-nos (1830 GX G30 only). Command: set trib-ptp-<name> tributary-disable-action laser-shut-off. Delay it with tributary-disable-holdoff-timer, 0..10000 ms, default 0 meaning hold-off disabled; it applies only when the TDA action is laser-turnoff, holding the optical signal until the timer expires. Related switches on the same object: near-end-tda enabled|disabled default disabled, tda-degrade-mode enabled|disabled default disabled, and forward-defect-trigger true|false default true, which decides whether a received client forward defect such as LF or ODU-AIS flows through to the line side or triggers an egress TDA action.
